page.layout: One page of text in a single column: a Latin verse passage in italics at the top, a horizontal rule, then a French poem with a heading "XI. GAL.", then a Latin poem under the heading "LAT.". The catchword sits at the lower right.

p.i: Exercetq; vagus error amabilis, Hic se quærit homo, uiuere dum cupit Hospes non sibi cognitus.
Umbrarum & celeres persequitur fugas Quæ finxit proprio Marte putans bona: Commentisque suum pectus inanibus Gaudet ꝑ scere[?] vanior.
Feriens præcipitem si trahit impetus, Si torquet rabies sæua libidinis Illum quis retrahet? Recta monentium Voces negligit impotens.

main_text.head: XI. GAL.
main_text.p: L'ESTRANGER estonné regarde & se pourmeine Par les antiquitez de la gloire Romaine: Il void les arcs rompus,& les marbres luisans Mutilez, massacrez par la fureur des ans: Il void pendante en l'air une moussue pierre Qui arme ses costez des longs bras du lierre: Et qui est-ce,dit-il,qui ici bas se fonde: Puis que le temps vainqueur triomphe de ce Monde?
main_text.head: LAT.
main_text.p: ANTIQUA prisca monstra superbiæ Gentis Quiritum, quum videt insolens

page.notes: The top passage is set in italic and begins mid-poem, so its first stanza continues from the previous page. The large initial L of the French poem is joined to "ESTRANGER" as printed. The "Hospes" at the lower right is the catchword, not text. "p scere" in the fourth line of the Latin verse is uncertain: the p carries an abbreviation mark, read here as ꝑ. The page number is printed as "IIO". Printed V for capital U (MVNDI, ANTIQVA, Vmbrarum, vne) is normalised to U/u by the rule. Scan quality is good; no illegible words.
